$comment: WO-6 casting tables — machine-readable transcription of final-plan.md Part 2 (per-role castings), Part 3.4 (review mandate + R0 matrix), Part 5.5 (pool states / degradation ladder), and the Q0 automatic triggers (seat 19). The registry (registry/classes.json) owns the taxonomy; this file owns who runs it at which rung under which pool state. Edit the plan first, then mirror here — router/router.js cross-checks this file against the registry at load and fails closed on any drift. Two entries are WO-6 defaults the plan leaves unstated, marked unstatedInPlan.

effortLadders.$comment: Effort ladders differ per vendor (§2.0); 'off' is Haiku thinking-off; specials are dispatch-time values the Conductor seat carries.

poolStateLadder.$comment: §5.5, evaluated per bucket by the Quartermaster; the Conductor announces every rung change. No rung edits the mandatory set. 'Exhausted' is the exhaustion-matrix state past Red (allowance gone or hard-throttled out).

behavior.Amber: Authoring on this bucket re-casts to the healthy pool's mirrors, per role; review unchanged (last thing to sacrifice). P15 gate arms: below 40% AU-opus, no Opus dispatch without Quartermaster confirmation
behavior.Orange: Authoring on this bucket suspended; ceiling seats deferred (AU-fable stops first); only review, verification and in-flight completion draw
behavior.Red: Only calls that close already-authored changes. Mandatory classes whose cross-family direction needs this bucket do not close (wait / named human / park). Preferred classes may take the disclosed degraded path. Irreversible work waits, unconditionally
behavior.Exhausted: Per the exhaustion matrix: T0 work and cross-family-reviewable closure continue on the healthy pool; consequential closure needing this family waits or goes to a named human

reserve.$comment: P0's dynamic review reserve (seat 24) with WO-2's measured numbers. required = (forecast mandatory-review draw + forecast incident draw) × (1 + uncertaintyBuffer), floored at max(floorFractionOfBucket, cost of two gate-class reviews).
reserve.twoGateClassReviewsCostSource: WO-2 throughput probe 2026-08-28: 20 gate-class reviews drew ~3 percentage points of the weekly Codex window (~8%→11%)

liveness.$comment: §3.4 deployment gate (P10), settled by WO-2 — the mandate is active on the pinned cross-vendor review lane.

mandatoryReview.$comment: §3.4 — the set that can never degrade; fixed at design time, no degradation rung edits it.
unavailableOptions: named human expert review recorded in the ledger
park unmerged with HOLD: cross-family review unavailable

reviewMatrix.$comment: R0's computed casting (seat 21): family(reviewer) ∉ families(author + co-authors), evaluated at dispatch from the recorded family set. The Terra T1 lane is qualification-gated on WO-12f (not yet run) — Sol · high until the flag flips, and any pass is provisional with live monitoring.

degradedSameFamilyCandidates.$comment: Preferred-band degraded path only (§3.4): fresh-context, different-model, same-family review + mandatory Verifier, review.cross_family = false disclosed.

q0Triggers.$comment: Seat 19's automatic triggers — policy, not discretion. The scheduler creates Q0 when the implementation order is created; a missing required Q0 order blocks the work. Q0 is always Director-created, never implementer-spawned.

primary.note: the interactive session model IS the Conductor; no bootstrap layer

mirror.note: activated from a signed control checkpoint
restrictions: may not semantically close OpenAI-authored T2/T3 artifacts
may not author-and-approve the same plan
may not override an Anthropic verdict

Conductor.neverReason: owner ruling 2026-08-28: Opus holds no USER-DIALOGUE seat; never any cheap tier (judgment seat, P4)

nebulous.note: especially complex, nebulous, or ambiguous goals; owner judgment at intake; Max-or-above Anthropic seat

exhaustionFallback.note: when the Codex allowance is exhausted

mirror.note: the opposite family of whichever primary is cast; under the Sol default this is the Anthropic lane

Architect.securityRouteFilter: security-sensitive planning is a hard route-filter to the Sol lane — never the Fable casting (silent classifier fallback on cyber/bio topics)

Synthesizer.neverReason: never any cheap tier — the merge is the longest-horizon synthesis in the system

Scout.shapeNote: scoped maximum — never haystack (§ seat 4); truncation or unexhausted surface auto-reclassifies to N2/I0

mirror.note: pool-aware — N0 stays on Haiku by default to protect the OpenAI review reserve

deep.note: deep, contradictory retrieval chains or safety/architecture/procurement-relevant research

Researcher.neverReason: the corpus is a haystack by definition
Researcher.$comment: `never` binds the CASTING (the engine doing the work, e.g. GPT-5.6 Sol) — not a thin OpenAI-launcher file's own `model: haiku` shell, which carries no judgment and is a different actor from the casting it dispatches to

mirror.note: covers corpora up to ~1M tokens — full mirror, not partial
preferred when the defect is environment- or tool-loop-shaped; wrong for race hunts — the concurrency blind spot

ceiling.note: trail cold and blocking, or after two failed hunts with different hypotheses

noMirrorFor.videoAudio: declared no-mirror exception: raw video and audio go below the model layer — deterministic frame extraction + local speech-to-text, else typed UNAVAILABLE; never a silent narrowing to stills

tacticalRaise.note: one effort raise on the same casting, once (tactical stall)

mirror.note: strategy-level stall crosses families — a different lineage brings a different prior; ordering provisional pending WO-12e

Runner.shapeNote: packet — the hardest constraint in the roster, dispatcher-enforced

mirror.note: choose by pool room and parent cache locality; never mix vendors inside one cached prefix

preferredBounded.note: bounded, short-horizon, fully-specified, deterministically-verifiable orders only; Luna never receives under-specified work

primary.note: orders expected to run longer or whose spec is thinner than Luna's bar

Builder.guardrail: Luna never receives under-specified work — the guardrail survives the promotion

effortPoint2.note: one tier, two effort points — not two rungs of the ladder

ceiling.note: Max seat only; reached only after both Opus effort points bounced AND the diagnosis is ceiling, not under-specified

reversibleT1.note: only reversible T1 extraction/transformation/query sub-work AFTER the integrity design is fixed by the primary or A0

noMirrorFor.irreversible: declared no-mirror exception: the irreversible half. Pool pressure changes WHEN T2/T3 data work is scheduled, never WHO prepares it; if the Anthropic pool is exhausted, irreversible data work waits

closing.note: dispatched as a separate READ-ONLY order — no WRITE-TREE; an edit would make it a co-author and disqualify it from closing; always a different family from the generator

critic.note: rare — passes every check and still looks wrong; effort unstated in the plan, high adopted to match the E6 critic (WO-6 default)

noMirrorFor.primary: declared no-mirror exception, unstated in the plan: final-plan.md Part 2 seat 15 names no authoring mirror for the E5 primary — closing (Opus 5, high) is dispatched as a SEPARATE READ-ONLY order (an edit would make it a co-author and disqualify it from closing) and critic (Fable 5, ceiling) is a rare global-critique ceiling; neither is an authoring substitution target for the Sol primary. Pool outage on the primary casting waits or returns typed UNAVAILABLE.

critic.note: global visual critique; runs last and rarely

mirror.note: the agentic engine loop (build-run-screenshot-adjust) rather than the geometry itself
strong at find-and-harden, weaker on exploitation reasoning

Red Team.neverReason: a policy fact, not a capability judgment: silent classifier fallback on cyber topics — a security review routed there may be answered by a different model with nothing saying so. Hard route-filter

Refactorer.shapeNote: unstated in the plan; repo+haystack adopted (the consumer census is the point of the Terra 1M window) — WO-6 default

Test Designer.castRule: cast opposite the implementation author's family; a human-authored implementation takes whichever pool is healthier, tie → the Anthropic lane (protects the OpenAI review reserve, Part 5)
Test Designer.directorCreated: Q0 is always Director-created, never spawned by the implementer — the independence is the point

crossFamilyByConstruction.reason: mirror substitution is unlawful by construction — the seat is cast opposite the implementation author's family, so substituting the other lane under pool outage would place the test designer same-family with the author, violating the invariant. router.js has no special-cased Q0 outage handling: rung selection (router.js:417-430) always names vsAnthropicAuthor or vsOpenaiAuthor from implementationAuthorFamily, and this role carries no `mirror` rung, so when that rung's bucket cannot take the authoring purpose, cast()'s generic degradation fallback (router.js:475-488) finds role.rungs.mirror undefined, the Data-Engineer-only reversibleT1 fallback does not apply, and it falls through to the final refusal: outcome WAIT, reason 'no lawful casting: <model> bucket at <state> ... and the role declares no mirror for this work' (router.js:485-488). Outage means wait, or a typed UNAVAILABLE at the caller — never a same-family substitution.

Doc Writer.shapeNote: unstated in the plan; repo adopted (runbooks and migration guides read the tree) — WO-6 default

primary.note: routine developer documentation tied to verified behavior

deliverable.note: deliverable-grade documents, public contracts, migration guides

ceiling.note: documents that are themselves deliverables; Max seat only

mirror.note: declared non-equivalent (~12 Elo behind on knowledge-work artifacts): add a cross-family register/over-claiming read; deliverable-grade documents wait for the primary pool rather than shipping on the mirror

Doc Writer.neverReason: both identified as their family's weak writers in a blind prose panel; bad docs are not caught by tests and are read for years

Reviewer.computedRule: family(reviewer) ∉ families(author + co-authors), evaluated at dispatch from the ledger's recorded family set — the full co-author set, never just the original author. Use reviewer(), never cast()

Sweeper.castRule: never the instance that performed the fan-out; prefer the opposite family from the author

modelAssist.note: checklist classification against explicit yes/no criteria only, cheapest tier with pool room, ensemble votes where a wrong vote must be absorbed; every result records model-assist provenance
deterministic code over the ledger; cheapest-tier model only for summarization
